# @kayjs/mail Reference

> Zero-dependency email delivery (Resend HTTP or custom transport) with a dev-only HTML/JSON outbox preview.

## Imports

- `@kayjs/mail`: `createMailer`, `resend`, `MailNotConfiguredError`; types `Mailer`, `MailerOptions`, `MailPreviewOptions`, `MailMessage`, `SentMail`, `MailAddress`, `MailTransport`.

## Setup (`createMailer(options?)`)

`createMailer()` returns a single object that is both the `KayPlugin` (register in `kay.config.ts`) and the handle routes/actions call `mail.send()` on:

- `from`: default sender (`string | { name, address }`, falls back to `process.env.MAIL_FROM` or `'noreply@localhost'`).
- `to`: default recipient(s) (falls back to `process.env.MAIL_TO` or `'dev@localhost'`).
- `transport`: `MailTransport` (`{ send(mail: SentMail): Promise<void> }`). Defaults to `resend()` when `process.env.RESEND_API_KEY` is set.
- `optional`: when `false`/omitted, calling `send()` in `NODE_ENV=production` without a transport throws `MailNotConfiguredError`.
- `previewRoute`: dev outbox URL (default `'/_kay/mail'`). `preview: false` disables the preview.

## Mounted Routes (dev/test only — never in production)

- `GET /_kay/mail` — HTML outbox viewer (HTML bodies rendered in sandboxed `<iframe>`s).
- `GET /_kay/mail.json` — `{ count, messages }` JSON dump of captured messages (up to 100 in memory; production keeps no copy).

## Handle & Transport API

- `await mail.send({ from?, to?, replyTo?, subject, text?, html? })` → `SentMail` (`{ id, from, to, replyTo?, subject, text?, html?, sentAt }`).
- `mail.isConfigured()`: `boolean`. `mail.outbox`: `SentMail[]`. `mail.clearOutbox()`.
- `resend({ apiKey?, endpoint? })`: built-in Resend HTTP transport using `fetch()`.
- Works directly as `createAuth({ mailer: mail })` with `@kayjs/auth`.

## Snippet

```ts
// src/mail.ts (and register `plugins: [mail]` in kay.config.ts)
import { createMailer, resend } from '@kayjs/mail'

export const mail = createMailer({
  from: 'App <noreply@example.com>',
  transport: process.env.RESEND_API_KEY ? resend() : undefined,
})

// In an action or route:
await mail.send({ to: 'ada@example.com', subject: 'Welcome', text: 'Hello!' })
```
